newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SEEN LOWER ON LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SEEN LOWER ON LIQUIDITY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely stable on Monday morning with dealers expecting them to be depressed during the week on the back of liquidity.
The central Reserve Bank, forecasting an surplus of money at the end of Monday trade, auctioned 200 million worth of 91-day treasury bills at an average discount rate of 24.32 percent.
The central bank bills were being sold on the secondary market at 24.25 percent while call money was at 24 percent.

NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 26.5 percent and sold at 25 and bank acceptance bills were at 25.5 percent (buying) but softer at 24.30 percent from 25 on the selling side.
Last week, market analysts said rates were likely to dip slightly on the back of a World Bank announcement that it would resume financial aid for the country's economic reform programme.
They added that a slip in year-on-year inflation to 19.1 percent in July from 21.4 percent in June would also dampen the rates.
